terms.it: La casa e le sue stanze
terms.pt: A casa e os seus cômodos

en.title: The house and its rooms
en.summary: Describing a home: the rooms, the furniture, and the grammar of there is, there are, a and the.

sections.title: About this lesson
paragraphs: Talking about where you live is one of the first things you do in a new language. In this lesson Maria describes her flat. You will see two small words that cause many mistakes, a and the, and the phrase there is, which says what a place contains.

sections.title: In context
paragraphs: I live in a small flat in Manchester. The flat is on the top floor. There is a living room, a kitchen, a bathroom and two bedrooms. The living room is next to the kitchen. In the living room there is a sofa and a table. There are two chairs near the window. The sofa is blue, and the table is old. The bathroom is small, but it is clean. My bedroom is at the back of the flat. There is a bed in it, and there is a lamp on the desk. The lamp is new. My neighbours live on the floor below.

sections.title: Grammar notes
paragraphs: **1. A or the.** Use a (or an before a vowel sound) when you mention something for the first time. Use the when both people know which thing you mean. In the text, **a lamp** is new information, and **The lamp is new** is about that same lamp. A plural word with no article, such as chairs, also names something for the first time. See Introduction to Grammar: Articles and determiners.

| Use | Article | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| first mention, one thing | a or an | **There is a lamp on the desk.** |
| a thing both people know | the | **The lamp is new.** |
| first mention, more than one | no article | **There are chairs near the window.** |

**2. There is and there are.** To say that a place contains something, use there is with one thing and there are with more than one. The place comes after. For a question, turn it round: **Is there a balcony?** For the negative, add not: **There isn't a garden.** See Introduction to Grammar: Present tense, being and having.

sections.title: Notice
paragraphs: The small words that show where things are come before the noun. Learn them with the picture of a room in your head.

| Word | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| in | inside | **in the kitchen** |
| on | touching the top of a surface | **on the desk** |
| next to | beside | **next to the kitchen** |
| near | close to | **near the window** |
| at the back of | behind, in the far part | **at the back of the flat** |

sections.title: Culture note
paragraphs: In Britain many people live in a terraced house, a semi-detached house (a semi) or a flat. In British English the floor at street level is the ground floor and the next one up is the first floor. In American English the floor at street level is the first floor.
